content:
sara-support: Hi team — customer AcmeCorp reporting p99 spikes (~3s) for EU users since ~03:40 UTC. They say requests end up in us-west. attaching trace id and sample req ids. customer says region header = eu-west. https://console.redwood.com/traces/trace-0a1b2c

mike-sre: looking. can you paste one of the raw request ids and headers?

sara-support: sample req: req-0a1b2c. headers:
```
:authority: api.redwood.ai
x-region: eu-west
x-client-id: acme-123
user-agent: acme/1.2 curl/7.68.0
```

anita-runtime: saw a similar pattern last week when region_fallback kicked in. can we get the trace flame or hop list?

sara-support: pasted the trace hops (condensed):
```
trace-0a1b2c:
 - ingress-eu-west (proxy)
 - global-router-1 (route-decider)
 - us-west-edge-02 (selected backend)
 - gpu-pool-us-west-3 (model host)
```
Customer also included a p99 graph showing spike at 03:39-03:42 UTC.

trace-bot: Automated analysis: routing policy "region_fallback" triggered for trace-0a1b2c. Selected target: us-west (capacity_shard=0). Healthcheck window for eu-west: 03:38:50-03:42:10 => 0 healthy backends.

mike-sre: that bot output suggests eu-west pool had no healthy backends. can someone pull healthcheck events for eu-west around 03:35-03:45? also need autoscaler logs.

anita-runtime: pulled healthcheck timeline: multiple short 503s from host eu-host-7, then whole pool went marked unhealthy by router. autoscaler kicked but pods failed to recover quickly due to image pull delay on a subset of nodes.

jun-support: customer confirmed workaround: pinning region in requests (x-region: eu-west-pin) lowers latency immediately. they're asking for root cause summary and ETA for fix.

mike-sre: intermediate hypothesis: transient node failures in eu-west -> router marks pool unhealthy -> routing policy falls back to global/us-west -> cross-region hop increases p99. Need to verify: 1) node OOM/kernel messages, 2) image-pull throttling, 3) autoscaler backoff logs. I'll open an incident.

oncall: acknowledged. I'm attaching initial incident: INC-2026-0423-77. Assigned to @mike-sre and @anita-runtime. First steps: collect node syslogs for eu-host-7..eu-host-10, check kube events for imagePullBackOff, and review recent capacity reconciles.

anita-runtime: quick note — there was a package registry flake in eu region at ~03:37 which could explain image pulls failing and delaying autoscaler. correlating events now.

trace-bot: Helpful links: Trace UI: https://console.redwood.com/traces/trace-0a1b2c, Health timeline: https://console.redwood.com/health/eu-west?from=1779000000&to=1779004000

mike-sre: action items for this thread: 
- [ ] collect diagnostics tarball (metrics + syslogs) from eu-host-7..10
- [ ] extract autoscaler reconcile logs around 03:30-03:50
- [ ] validate router config doesn't prematurely mark pool zero-capacity on short 503 windows
- [ ] push hotfix: reduce fallback sensitivity or increase minimum healthy threshold for 5m window

jun-support: I've updated the support ticket and told AcmeCorp we're investigating and provided the pinning workaround. they appreciate quick workaround but want permanent fix.

sara-support: adding note to ticket: customer-supplied traces + our analysis + workaround. will update when incident PR / rollback policy decided. :thumbsup:

oncall: I'll follow up in the incident channel with timeline and ETA. leaving this thread open for support updates only.

mike-sre: thanks — I'll post incident link and root cause once we have logs.

sara-support: thanks everyone, closing customer-facing loop for now. will post final update.
